Action Plan:
1. Start ibuprofen for acute headache (ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented). Continue paracetamol as needed (paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented).
2. Advise one week off work (self-certify) to reduce stress; patient to consider taking this time off.
3. Offer counselling — provide local counselling service link for patient self-referral.
4. Advise sleep and hydration measures: aim for 7–8 hours sleep nightly and 1.5–2.0 L fluids per day (excluding coffee/tea).
5. Arrange follow-up in one week to reassess symptoms. If no improvement, consider blood tests or other investigations.
6. Advise to contact clinic sooner if symptoms worsen or new concerning features develop; clinician will leave a link in notes describing headache red flags.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: New-onset, severe left-sided headache since awakening this morning (~05:30); headache persists at time of consult.
- Symptom characteristics:
  - Unilateral left-sided head pain; described as “headachy.”
  - Woke patient from sleep; initially felt dizzy on rising but dizziness has subsided.
  - Mild light sensitivity causing eye soreness.
  - No fever, no nausea, no neck stiffness.
  - Slight improvement when lying down after initial discomfort.
  - Paracetamol taken this morning (paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented); patient reports minimal relief.
- Onset/duration/progression: Started this morning; woke patient at ~05:30; ongoing throughout the day.
- Past headache history: Prior headaches described as less severe and typically across the front of the head (not strictly unilateral).
- Past medical history: Anxiety diagnosed previously (approximately 2 years).
- Medications: Sertraline — dose/route/frequency not documented; Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented (taken today).
- Allergies: None known to patient.
- Social history:
  - Lives with partner.
  - Non-smoker.
  - Has a cat.
  - Exercise: runs ~3 times per week.
  - Diet: described as “okay.”
  - Work stress: increased workload and late nights for ~2 months.
- Family history: Mother with anxiety; no known family migraines.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed (telephone/video consult); doctor documented inability to examine the patient directly.
- No vital signs or diagnostic test results available.
- No investigations performed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Tension-type headache.
   - Differential diagnosis: Migraine.
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; if no improvement at 1-week follow-up, consider blood tests or further investigations.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Start ibuprofen (ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Continue paracetamol as needed (paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Non-pharmacologic: ensure 7–8 hours sleep nightly; drink 1.5–2.0 L fluids/day (excluding coffee/tea); avoid dehydration and sleep deprivation.
   - Relevant referrals: Provide link to counselling service for self-referral.
   - Follow-up: Reassess in 1 week; earlier contact if worsening or new concerning features. Clinician to leave link to headache “danger signs” in notes.

2. Anxiety / Work-related stress:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Anxiety disorder (history of anxiety).
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A.
   - Investigations planned: None.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Continue current sertraline (sertraline — dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Recommend counselling referral (link to local service provided) to address work-related stress.
     - Consider taking one week off work (self-certified) to reduce stress and assess symptom improvement.
   - Relevant referrals: Counselling service (self-referral link to be provided).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, temperature), neurological examination findings, exact medication doses/routes/frequencies for ibuprofen, paracetamol, and sertraline, allergy verification beyond patient report, and any prior headache workup history.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Audible and clear; occasional pauses and filler words but clinically relevant information captured.
